topic: Qualitative Characteristics of Images in Mirrors and Lenses
key_concepts: Light is electromagnetic radiation made of photons and travels as waves
Light travels in straight lines called rays and can move through a vacuum
Light can be absorbed, transmitted, reflected, or scattered when it strikes matter
Law of reflection: incident ray, reflected ray, and normal lie in the same plane
Angle of incidence equals angle of reflection
Regular reflection occurs on smooth surfaces; diffuse reflection occurs on rough surfaces
Plane mirror images are virtual, same size, same orientation, and same distance behind the
Concave mirrors can form real, inverted images that are magnified, diminished, or same siz
Convex mirrors always form virtual, erect, diminished images
Concave lenses produce smaller upright images and correct nearsightedness
Convex lenses are thicker at the center than at the edges
